# A subscription

A subscription is one input answered by a stream: the state as it stands when the stream opens, then each change as it happens, then an end. Every Nexus declares, carries and serves it the same way.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    s["the subscriber"] -- "one input, on a connection of its own" --> n["the Nexus"]
    n -- "Opened: the state as it stands" --> s
    n -- "Changed: each change, as it happens" --> s
    n -- "Lagged: the state anew, when the subscriber fell behind" --> s
    n -- "Ended: why the stream is over" --> s
```

## In Ethos

Stream is a type Ethos knows without import, as it knows Vector and Option. It takes two types: the state the stream opens with, and the change it then carries. An output whose payload is a Stream is answered as a stream.

```ethos
Signal
[ harness:[ Observed Event State ]
  flow:[ FlowId ] ]
[ Subscribe ]
[ Subscribed.Stream<Vector<Observed> Changed> ]
[ Changed.{ FlowId Event State } ]
```

Subscribe is answered by Subscribed, a stream that opens with every session as observed now and then carries each Changed.

## In Rust

A Stream is a futures-core Stream of frames. The frame is the one type that travels: it says what each item is, so the opening, a lag and the end are typed, and nothing is told by a closed connection alone.

```rust
pub enum Frame<State, Change> {
    Opened(State),
    Changed(Change),
    Lagged(State),
    Ended(Ending),
}
pub enum Ending { Closed, Failed }
pub struct Stream<State, Change> {
    frames: Pin<Box<dyn futures_core::Stream<Item = Frame<State, Change>> + Send>>,
}
impl<State, Change> futures_core::Stream for Stream<State, Change> {
    type Item = Frame<State, Change>;
    fn poll_next(self: Pin<&mut Self>, context: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Self::Item>> { /* the inner stream's */ }
}
```

Opened is always the first frame and comes once. Lagged carries the whole state again: a subscriber that fell behind lost changes, and the state is what makes it right. Ended is always the last frame.

The subscriber's side, generated with the Signal:

```rust
let mut stream = harness.subscribe()?;
while let Some(frame) = stream.next().await {
    match frame {
        Frame::Opened(observed) | Frame::Lagged(observed) => record.replace(observed),
        Frame::Changed(changed) => record.after(changed),
        Frame::Ended(ending) => break,
    }
}
```

## On the socket

A stream rides the connection that opened it, one stream to a connection. Each frame is signalized and written with the same framing as every reply of the Nexus: a length, then the archive. The length's byte order and the frame capacity are the signal library's, one value for every Nexus, the capacity a configuration. After Ended the Nexus closes the connection. A subscriber that wants no more closes it, and the Nexus forgets that subscriber. A subscriber whose connection dropped subscribes again and has the state.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    f["a Frame"] -- "signalize" --> a["its archive"]
    a -- "length, then the archive" --> c["the opening connection"]
    c -- "restore" --> g["the Frame, at the subscriber"]
```

## Serving it

What can be subscribed to is Subscribable: it names its state and its change, and gives its state as it stands. A Publisher holds the subscribers of one Subscribable, inside the Kameo actor that owns the state.

```ethos
Traits
[ Subscribable.{ []
                 [ State Change ]
                 []
                 [ state.[ State ] ] } ]
```

```rust
pub trait Subscribable { type State; type Change; fn state(&self) -> Self::State; }
pub struct Capacity(pub Integer);
pub struct Publisher<State, Change> {
    changes: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<Change>,
    capacity: Capacity,
}
pub trait Publishing<State, Change> {
    fn publish(&self, change: Change);
    fn open(&self, state: State) -> Stream<State, Change>;
}
```

open gives one subscriber its Stream: Opened with the state, then every change published after it. publish hands one change to every open stream and waits for none of them. The Capacity is how many changes a subscriber may fall behind, a configuration; a subscriber past it receives Lagged with the state as it then stands and goes on from there. No subscriber slows the Nexus or another subscriber, and none is dropped for being slow.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    o["an operation changes Memory, and Memory answers Succeeded"] -- "publish: the change" --> p["Publisher"]
    p -- "to every open stream" --> s["a subscriber's Stream"]
    s -- "within its capacity" --> c["Changed"]
    s -- "past its capacity: the backlog is dropped" --> l["Lagged, with the state as it stands"]
```

## Where a change comes from

A change is published by the operation that made it, at the moment Memory answers that it succeeded. Nothing is found by asking again on a timer: a Nexus whose state is another Nexus's subscribes to that Nexus and publishes what the stream brings.

```rust
impl Operable for Record {
    fn operate(&self, nexus: &mut Nexus) -> Recorded {
        let answer = nexus.memory.change(self);
        if let Answer::Succeeded = answer { nexus.publisher.publish(Changed::from(self)) }
        Recorded
    }
}
```
